commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Perf] Skip masked-out context tiles for sliding-window models in Triton prefix-prefill
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

- Skip reads of out-of-window KV tiles in sliding-window prefix prefill on ROCm.
- It applies to vLLM sliding-window models such as Gemma 2/3, Mistral/Zephyr, Cohere2, Granite, and GLM-5.x DSpark drafts.

## Claims

On gfx942 (MI300X, MI325X), ROCm 10.0, Triton 3.8.0:

- Up to **38.37x** kernel time at a 32,000-token context with a 512-token window
  and head size 256 (MI300X, KV cache > 2 GB).
- **1.69x** TTFT at 32,000-token prompts for zephyr-7b-beta (MI300X), **2.21x**
  for gemma-3-1b-it (MI325X).
- **1.39x / 1.38x** lower inter-token latency for GLM-5.2-FP8 / GLM-5.3 with
  DSpark drafts, whose sliding-window layers run this kernel on every
  verification step (8x MI325X, TP8).
- Bit-identical output to the kernel without this PR in every configuration
  tested. Where nothing is skipped, kernel time is 0.99-1.05x and TTFT at
  2,048-token prompts is unchanged.
- No new option, env var or kernel variant.

## Validation

One MI325X, `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-083fbac021348c2c7af8a7bc71ba18199d0dd7a4`:

```bash
docker run -it --rm --device /dev/kfd --device /dev/dri --group-add video \
  --security-opt seccomp=unconfined -e HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 -v "$PWD/tests":/work/tests:ro \
  -v "$PWD/pyproject.toml":/work/pyproject.toml:ro -w /work --entrypoint bash \
  vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-083fbac021348c2c7af8a7bc71ba18199d0dd7a4
curl -sL https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63867.diff -o /tmp/pr.diff
(cd /usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages && git apply -p1 --include='vllm/*' /tmp/pr.diff)
python3 -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider --noconftest tests/kernels/attention/test_prefix_prefill.py
```

`402 passed, 64 skipped`. Two tests are new:

- `test_contexted_kv_attention_window_shorter_than_context` fills unused KV slots
  with NaN; covers KV page sizes 16, 32 and 48, head sizes 128 and 256, and a
  window that starts at the last key of a tile. It passes 36/36 with and without
  this PR. It fails 8/36 when the skip is not page-aligned, 12/36 when the start
  is one key late, and 6/36 without the clamp.
- `test_contexted_kv_attention_window_v_cache_over_2gb` uses a V cache of 2 GiB
  plus one page, so head size 256 takes unroll 4 on gfx942. It passes with and
  without this PR and fails with the block-table offset removed.

### Kernel time

`context_attention_fwd`, one MI300X, one sequence, KV page size 16, median of 3
repeats. Triton uses 64-bit addressing for KV caches over 2 GB, as in serving,
and buffer loads for smaller ones.

| config | context / query | without PR, > 2 GB | speedup, > 2 GB | speedup, < 2 GB |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| bf16, 32 Q / 8 KV heads, hs 128, W=4096 | 1,024 / 6 | 105.6 µs | 0.99x | 0.99x |
| | 2,048 / 2,048 | 578.6 µs | 1.00x | 1.00x |
| | 14,336 / 2,048 | 2603.8 µs | 3.57x | 3.44x |
| | 30,000 / 2,000 | 5319.6 µs | 7.24x | 6.95x |
| fp16, 8 Q / 8 KV heads, hs 128, W=2048 | 1,024 / 6 | 108.8 µs | 1.01x | 1.00x |
| | 8,192 / 6 | 745.1 µs | 3.74x | 3.58x |
| | 32,000 / 6 | 2873.8 µs | 14.32x | 13.98x |
| bf16, 4 Q / 1 KV heads, hs 256, W=512 | 256 / 6 | 74.2 µs | 1.05x | 1.39x |
| | 0 / 2,048 | 262.6 µs | 0.99x | 1.44x |
| | 8,192 / 6 | 1095.8 µs | 10.00x | 11.30x |
| | 32,000 / 6 | 4216.2 µs | 38.37x | 42.65x |
| bf16, 64 Q / 64 KV heads, hs 64, W=2048 | 2,048 / 8 | 169.6 µs | 0.99x | 0.99x |
| | 32,000 / 8 | 2474.4 µs | 14.25x | 14.03x |
| bf16, 32 Q / 8 KV heads, hs 128, no window | 8,192 / 2,048 | 1570.2 µs | 1.00x | 1.00x |
| bf16, 4 Q / 1 KV heads, hs 256, no window | 8,192 / 2,048 | 1336.6 µs | 1.00x | 1.00x |

### Serving

```bash
vllm serve HuggingFaceH4/zephyr-7b-beta --attention-backend ROCM_ATTN --dtype bfloat16 \
  --max-model-len 32768 --max-num-batched-tokens 2048 --seed 0
vllm bench serve --model HuggingFaceH4/zephyr-7b-beta --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len 32000 --random-output-len 64 --random-range-ratio 0 --ignore-eos \
  --max-concurrency 1 --num-prompts 5
python3 tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000
```

zephyr-7b-beta (W=4096), one MI300X, 3 servers per arm, one at a time, median
across servers:

| prompt / output tokens, concurrency | TTFT | TPOT | output throughput |
|---|---|---|---|
| 32,000 / 64, 1 | 2534.0 -> 1503.3 ms (1.69x) | 65.5 -> 65.5 ms | 9.6 -> 11.4 tok/s |
| 16,384 / 128, 4 | 2677.1 -> 1832.5 ms (1.46x) | 71.4 -> 61.5 ms | 44.2 -> 53.3 tok/s |
| 2,048 / 128, 16 | 405.7 -> 404.4 ms | 20.4 -> 20.3 ms | 680.4 -> 683.2 tok/s |

gemma-3-1b-it (W=512, head size 256), one MI325X, same commands with
`unsloth/gemma-3-1b-it` and 5 / 8 / 32 prompts per row, 3 servers per arm,
interleaved, median across servers:

| prompt / output tokens, concurrency | TTFT | TPOT | output throughput |
|---|---|---|---|
| 32,000 / 64, 1 | 1041.1 -> 471.8 ms (2.21x) | 73.36 -> 73.39 ms | 11.30 -> 12.57 tok/s |
| 16,384 / 128, 4 | 941.6 -> 672.8 ms (1.40x) | 46.64 -> 43.34 ms | 71.78 -> 79.12 tok/s |
| 2,048 / 128, 16 | 91.0 -> 86.9 ms | 8.92 -> 8.86 ms | 1607.8 -> 1619.3 tok/s |

A second MI325X reproduces the direction independently, arms differing only in
`prefix_prefill.py`: zephyr-7b-beta 32,000 / 64, 1 goes 2276.5 -> 1258.4 ms
(1.81x), 16,384 / 128, 4 goes 2618.7 -> 1822.0 ms (1.44x), 2,048 / 128, 16 goes
474.0 -> 468.7 ms; gemma-3-1b-it 32,000 / 64, 1 goes 1146.8 -> 650.2 ms (1.76x).
Baseline rounds repeat to 0.3-2.2% at 16,384 and 32,000 tokens. The 2,048 cell
spreads 21.8% between two identical baseline runs, so read its median
(370.3 -> 369.1 ms, 1.00x), not its mean.

Greedy decode at temperature 0 with `--enforce-eager`, gemma-3-1b-it: generated
token ids and the full prompt-logprob vector are identical with and without this
PR at 1,024, 8,192 and 20,000 tokens, and at 20,512 tokens sharing a
20,000-token cached prefix.

### Accuracy

GSM8K, 5-shot, 1,319 questions, greedy, one run per server: 40.4 / 39.6 / 40.4%
without this PR and 39.4 / 39.6 / 40.1% with it (zephyr-7b-beta); 28.1 / 29.2 /
28.2% without and 28.9 / 28.4 / 28.4% with (gemma-3-1b-it). With speculative
decoding on GLM-5.3: 91.4 / 91.2% without and 90.8 / 90.5% with. On one pair of
servers, 49 questions were answered correctly only without this PR and 40 only
with it (exact McNemar p = 0.40).

GPQA and NIAH 128k: `unsloth/gemma-3-12b-it` (W=1024, head size 256, 128k
context), one MI325X per arm, `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-7c3a9302f5ac2441ad199134129e973d22a46797`;
without this PR is the same image.

```bash
vllm serve unsloth/gemma-3-12b-it --attention-backend ROCM_ATTN --max-model-len 131072 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":0}' --seed 0
lm_eval --model local-completions \
  --model_args model=unsloth/gemma-3-12b-it,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/completions,tokenized_requests=False,num_concurrent=32 \
  --tasks gpqa_diamond_zeroshot --seed 1234
lm_eval --model local-completions \
  --model_args model=unsloth/gemma-3-12b-it,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/completions,tokenized_requests=False,num_concurrent=4,max_length=131072,tokenizer=unsloth/gemma-3-12b-it,timeout=3600 \
  --tasks niah_single_1,niah_single_2,niah_multikey_1 \
  --metadata '{"max_seq_lengths":[131072]}' --limit 50 --seed 1234
```

| task | without PR | with PR |
|---|---|---|
| gpqa_diamond_zeroshot (acc) | 0.3939 ± 0.0348 | 0.3939 ± 0.0348 |
| niah_single_1, 131072 | 1.00 | 1.00 |
| niah_single_2, 131072 | 1.00 | 1.00 |
| niah_multikey_1, 131072 | 0.64 | 0.66 |

NIAH uses 50 prompts per task. `niah_multikey_1` differs by one prompt.

GLM-5.2-FP8 with the DSpark draft (5 tokens), TP8 on 8x MI300X, serve flags under
Speculative decoding, `nightly-96710245ece8fe57a0df3ea18cdc79cbb8ce93cf`; without
this PR is the same container. GPQA and NIAH use the `lm_eval` commands above with
`model=zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8`.

| task | without PR | with PR |
|---|---|---|
| GSM8K, 5-shot, 1,319 questions | 0.939 | 0.938 |
| gpqa_diamond_zeroshot (acc) | 0.5101 ± 0.0356 | 0.5000 ± 0.0356 |
| niah_single_1, 131072 | 1.00 | 1.00 |
| niah_single_2, 131072 | 1.00 | 1.00 |
| niah_multikey_1, 131072 | 1.00 | 1.00 |

GPQA differs by 2 of 198 questions, GSM8K by 1.

### Speculative decoding

```bash
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1 \
  VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_CUSTOM_AR=1 HSA_NO_SCRATCH_RECLAIM=1
vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8 --tensor-parallel-size 8 --block-size 64 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.83 --max-model-len 263168 --max-num-seqs 128 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --safetensors-load-strategy prefetch \
  --compilation-config '{"pass_config": {"fuse_norm_quant": true, "fuse_act_quant": true}, "custom_ops": ["+rms_norm", "+silu_and_mul"]}' \
  --hf-overrides '{"index_topk_freq": 8}' --reasoning-parser glm45 --tool-call-parser glm47 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice --no-enable-expert-parallel --enable-prefix-caching --trust-remote-code \
  --speculative-config '{"model": "RedHatAI/GLM-5.2-speculator.dspark", "num_speculative_tokens": 5, "method": "dspark", "draft_sample_method": "greedy", "enable_adaptive_verification": false}'
vllm bench serve --model zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8 --dataset-name custom --dataset-path <prompts>.jsonl \
  --custom-output-len 300 --num-prompts 16 --max-concurrency 1 --seed 101 --num-warmups 2 --ignore-eos

vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3 --tensor-parallel-size 8 --block-size 64 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.83 --max-model-len 65536 --max-num-seqs 128 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --safetensors-load-strategy prefetch \
  --enable-prefix-caching --trust-remote-code \
  --speculative-config '{"method": "dspark", "model": "RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-speculator.dspark", "num_speculative_tokens": 8}'
vllm bench serve --model zai-org/GLM-5.3 --dataset-name random --random-input-len 8192 \
  --random-output-len 1024 --random-range-ratio 0 --ignore-eos --max-concurrency 4 \
  --num-prompts 16 --num-warmups 2 --seed 1
```

8x MI325X, TP8, same nightly; without this PR is the same container. The drafts'
three sliding-window layers (W=2048, head size 64) select `ROCM_ATTN` and run
this kernel on every verification step. The targets' sparse MLA does not, so
TTFT does not move. 2 servers per arm, median of runs:

| model, prompts | input / output, concurrency, runs per arm | ITL | TPOT | TTFT | output throughput |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| GLM-5.2-FP8, text, 5 draft tokens | 32,012 / 300, 1, 4 | 23.84 -> 17.17 ms (1.39x) | 8.45 -> 6.31 ms | 1232.3 -> 1235.0 ms | 80.2 -> 97.6 tok/s |
| GLM-5.3, random, 8 draft tokens | 32,000 / 1,024, 1, 2 | 24.31 -> 17.56 ms (1.38x) | 24.32 -> 17.57 ms | 1964.2 -> 1964.1 ms | 38.5 -> 52.0 tok/s |
| | 8,192 / 1,024, 4, 4 | 24.30 -> 22.83 ms (1.06x) | 21.38 -> 19.41 ms | 485.5 -> 481.4 ms | 176.0 -> 185.9 tok/s |
| GLM-5.2-FP8, text, 5 draft tokens, 8x MI300X | 32,012 / 300, 1, 4 | 24.29 -> 17.75 ms (1.37x) | 9.23 -> 6.58 ms | 1475.0 -> 1475.4 ms | 70.8 -> 87.8 tok/s |

The MI300X row is one server per arm.

ITL varies by at most 0.4 ms within an arm. TPOT moves with the acceptance
length, which varies run to run in both arms: 2.53-2.81 without and 2.67-2.76
with this PR on GLM-5.2's text prompts (16 prompts sharing a 12,800-token
prefix), 1.00 and 1.20-1.35 on random prompts.

Bitwise check: gemma-3-1b-it with `unsloth/gemma-3-270m-it` as the draft model
(4 tokens), `--attention-backend ROCM_ATTN`, 16 text prompts of 30,000 tokens,
300 tokens each, on `nightly-5d35ce3934a7804b298559d2d99eec33792e1eb9`.
Generated token ids and logprobs are identical with and without this PR across
three servers with two passes each. Running both kernels on every
`context_attention_fwd` call of those servers (619,998 calls: target
verification, draft and chunked prefill) gave identical bits.

## Details

- `prefix_prefill.py`: adds `CTX_SKIP_ALIGN`, the window-derived loop start, the
  `B_Loc_ctx` block-table offset and the unroll gate. `test_prefix_prefill.py`:
  parametrises the existing helper and adds the two tests above.
- A fully masked tile is already a no-op, so skipping it changes nothing.
  `SLIDING_WINDOW` is a constexpr, so layers without a sliding window compile to
  the same code as without this PR. The skip applies to Gemma2/3, Mistral/Zephyr,
  Cohere2, Granite and the GLM-5.x DSpark drafts.
- The loop counts from 0 over the remaining context with the block table offset,
  rather than starting at a runtime value: the latter is 4-16% slower at unroll 4
  on MI325X with KV caches over 2 GB, because the V-cache loads lose `dwordx4` in
  the 64-bit addressing variant.
- The start is clamped to the context length; with a start past the end, an
  unrolled `tl.range` still runs leftover iterations.
- On gfx942, sliding-window layers with head size above 128 use
  `num_unroll_cache=1` **only when the V cache fits in 2 GiB**. Unroll 4 spills
  there (296 vs 36 bytes of scratch per thread, 73 vs 8 VGPR spills) but issues
  fewer loads per iteration (62 vs 72), amortising the address computation.
  Within 2 GiB the kernel uses cheap 32-bit `buffer_load` and the spills are not
  repaid; past 2 GiB it uses 64-bit `global_load` and they are. At head size 256,
  5 interleaved rounds x 41 iterations, best round per arm:

  | case | V cache | unroll 1 | unroll 4 |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | W=512, ctx 8,192, q 6 | 0.004 GiB | **183.8 µs** | 194.3 µs |
  | W=512, ctx 32,000, q 6 | 0.015 GiB | **183.0 µs** | 194.3 µs |
  | W=4096, ctx 32,000, q 6 | 0.015 GiB | **589.1 µs** | 616.2 µs |
  | W=512, ctx 8,192, q 6 | 4.657 GiB | 205.4 µs | **196.2 µs** |
  | W=512, ctx 32,000, q 6 | 4.657 GiB | 204.3 µs | **195.9 µs** |
  | W=4096, ctx 32,000, q 6 | 4.657 GiB | 756.9 µs | **655.9 µs** |

  Other architectures keep unroll 4; compiled for gfx950, that variant has no
  scratch with or without this PR.
- The condition reads `v_cache.untyped_storage().size()`, not
  `v_cache.numel() * v_cache.element_size()`. `PagedAttention.split_kv_cache`
  returns `kv_cache[1]`, a view of the combined `(2, num_blocks, ...)` buffer,
  and Triton picks its addressing from the storage behind the pointer rather than
  the view's extent. Two V caches of identical shape (1.5 GiB each), one
  standalone and one such a view, compile differently: 78 `buffer_load` / 0
  `global_load` for the standalone, 43 / 248 for the view. Using the view's own
  extent would mispredict the addressing mode for every paged KV cache.
- `token_indices` keeps its original meaning, the absolute sequence position, and
  a separate `cache_indices` carries the block-table-relative value into
  `_paged_kv_cache_offsets`. Compiled ISA is unchanged, and the variable keeps a
  stable meaning for in-flight PRs that read it as an absolute position.
- Side effect on out-of-window pages: when the KV page size is a multiple of 32
  (ROCm's default is 64), `CTX_SKIP_ALIGN` equals the page size, so the first
  retained page always holds an in-window key and a freed page is never read.
  Measured on a local reproducer that fills freed pages with NaN, main produces
  NaN output at page/window 32/32, 16/32 and 16/16; this PR is clean at 32/32 and
  16/32 and still produces NaN at 16/16, where `lcm(32, 16) = 32` reaches back
  past a page boundary. That remaining case needs the masking in #53628; the two
  changes compose. This reproducer is not added here.
- **Limitation:** at long query lengths unroll 1 wins in both regimes. At head
  size 256, W=512, 32,000-token context with a 2,048-token query past 2 GB, this
  rule selects unroll 4 and is 9.4% slower than unroll 1 would be (386.7 vs
  353.2 µs). Only that one shape was measured, so no query-length term was added
  rather than fit a condition to a single point.
- The kernel table and the zephyr-7b-beta serving table were measured before the
  2 GiB condition was added. The final commit was re-measured against that head
  across 30 kernel configurations x 3 rounds; the worst ratio was 1.007x, so
  those tables still hold. In the kernel table only the `> 2 GB` head size 256
  rows change, and they improve.
- `_fwd_kernel_alibi` is untouched, so ALiBi layers get no benefit even with a
  sliding window.
- Each zephyr-7b-beta server compiles one `_fwd_kernel` variant at warmup and
  each gemma-3-1b-it server two (sliding and global layers); none compile another
  after the first 32,000-token prompt, the benchmarks or GSM8K, with and without
  this PR.
- MI355X (gfx950) was not measured. CI runs this test file on NVIDIA L4 and
  MI300; the new head size 256 cases are skipped on NVIDIA.
- Related: #62605 (same file; conflicts only on the grid line), #61433 (moves
  spec-decode drafts off `ROCM_ATTN`, after which the DSpark gain no longer
  applies), #60040 (prunes the same tiles through `compute_tile_loop_bounds` on
  its multimodal path), #53628 (masks the same region instead of skipping it),
  #62415 (closed; zeroed out-of-window V in this kernel). Depends on: None.

commits.pr_title: [Refactor][SleepMode] Expose CuMemBackend allocator hook
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`CuMemBackend` now resolves its platform allocator through a protected `_get_allocator()` hook that `suspend()`, `resume()`, and `discard()` share. The default implementation returns `get_mem_allocator_instance()`, so the built-in `cumem` backend behaves exactly as before; subclasses can override the hook to supply an allocator implementing the `MemAllocator` protocol.

Related: RFC #34303, which introduced the pluggable sleep-mode backend abstraction in #44074 and already anticipates platform-specific `CuMemBackend` subclasses (#45398).

## Claims

- One allocator resolution point in `CuMemBackend` instead of three copies of the lazy `get_mem_allocator_instance()` import.
- No behavior change for the built-in `cumem` backend: `_get_allocator()` returns exactly what the three lifecycle methods called before.
- Adds a documented extension point for downstream `CuMemBackend` subclasses.

## Validation

Source commit `d42f5008e1f66de2f6d94793b50cc08d1aae7af4`, based on `9e46474a7f`.

Static checks on the changed file:

```
ruff check vllm/device_allocator/sleep_mode_backend.py   -> All checks passed!
ruff format --check vllm/device_allocator/sleep_mode_backend.py -> 1 file already formatted
python tools/pre_commit/check_docstring_style.py vllm/device_allocator/sleep_mode_backend.py -> exit 0
git diff --check                                         -> clean
```

Behavior check (CPU only, worktree source, ad-hoc script that is not committed): a `CuMemBackend` subclass overriding `_get_allocator()` receives `sleep(("weights", "runtime", "cudagraph"), {42})`, `wake_up(["weights"])` and `discard(("weights",))` from the three lifecycle methods, and the default hook returns `get_mem_allocator_instance()`.

Repo pytest could not run on this host: the Windows environment cannot import the full test stack (Linux-only `uvloop`, plus a torch `c10.dll` load failure in the interpreter used for the suite). With `--noconftest`, `tests/v1/worker/test_sleep_mode_backend.py` gives `7 passed, 2 failed in 11.04s`; both failures are `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'uvloop'` raised from `vllm.v1.utils` while importing `gpu_worker`, unrelated to this change. CI should run the CPU unit tests for this file.

## Details

The three lifecycle methods used to inline `from vllm.device_allocator import get_mem_allocator_instance` and call the allocator directly. Moving resolution into `_get_allocator()` keeps the default path identical while giving a subclass a single override point for a different allocator, without duplicating `suspend`/`resume`/`discard` just to swap the allocator. `MemAllocator` is imported under `TYPE_CHECKING` only, and the module already has `from __future__ import annotations`.

This is intentionally a small, additive refactor: no in-tree consumer is added, and there is no user-visible surface (no CLI arg, config field, env var, model, hardware or default change), so no rendered-docs update is needed.

### Why this is not duplicating an existing PR

- Searched open PRs for `CuMemBackend`, `sleep_mode_backend`, `_get_allocator` and `allocator hook`. The open sleep-mode PRs (#47700, #55206, #63089, #63546, #58066) change CUDA graph tracking, pinned-host release, memory-growth assertions, failure paths or wake preparation; none adds an allocator resolution hook.
- #45398 (a `CuMemBackend` subclass for tag-selective offload) is closed, so it is not an open duplicate.

AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR (change, description and checks). The human submitter reviewed the diff and the results above.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][KVConnector] Split MLA kernel rows larger than the NIXL block into dense pages
commits.pr_body:
#### Overview

The NIXL connector registers a KV cache group incorrectly when the model runner picks a larger kernel block for that group than the block size NIXL picks across all groups. This PR registers such rows as dense NIXL pages when their layout allows it, and rejects the rest with an actionable error.

#### Root cause

- The runner selects a kernel block per KV cache group from that group's backends (`prepare_kernel_block_sizes`).
- NIXL selects one block size from the backends of *every* group (`_sync_block_size_with_kernel` → `select_common_block_size`), and applies one ratio (`_physical_blocks_per_logical_kv_block`) to all of them.
- When a backend in another group (e.g. a drafter's) only supports smaller blocks, a group can keep a kernel block (e.g. 128) larger than NIXL's (64). Its view is `[num_blocks, H, 128, C]`, so `stride(0)` spans two NIXL pages while NIXL's `num_blocks` is doubled. Registration then either:
  - raises `AssertionError: KV cache view cannot be partitioned into NIXL regions` (e.g. kernel 256 vs 64), or
  - silently registers whole storage rows when `num_blocks * block_stride` happens to match the storage span (e.g. kernel 128 vs 64, two layers per tensor). Transfers then address the wrong bytes.

This affects any attention type, not only MLA.

#### Example

`--block-size 128`, an MLA group whose backend supports `MultipleOf(16)`, and a drafter group whose backend only supports 64. MLA latent is 576 bf16 = 1152 B per token.

| | kernel block | MLA view | page | blocks |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| runner (MLA group) | 128 | `[N, 1, 128, 576]` | 147456 B (1 row) | `N` |
| NIXL (all groups) | 64 | — | 73728 B | `2N` |

NIXL maps logical block `b` to pages `2b` and `2b+1`, at `base + 2b * 73728` and `base + (2b+1) * 73728`. In the MLA view those are tokens 0-63 and 64-127 of row `b`, so dense 73728 B pages over the layer are exactly right. This PR registers them that way.

With 4 heads in `LBHNC`, row `b` is `[4, 128, C]`: its first half holds heads 0-1 for all 128 tokens, not tokens 0-63 for all heads. No page split matches a 64-token block there, so registration rejects it.

#### Fix

`_splits_kernel_rows` checks the view's geometry, not the spec type:
- **Token-major rows** (one head slot, as in MLA, or tokens outside heads as in `LBNHC`) are byte-identical to consecutive NIXL pages. They are registered as one dense region per layer with NIXL-sized pages. These are the same descriptors a group whose kernel block matches NIXL's would produce, so the handshake, the block-size ratio and the block-ID mapping are unchanged, and peers pair as before.
- **Head-major rows** (e.g. `LBHNC` with several heads) cannot be tiled by smaller pages. Registration raises `NotImplementedError` with the layer's geometry and suggests a smaller `--block-size` or `VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=LBNHC`.
- Block-outermost (packed) layouts are skipped: the runner never splits their blocks. Mamba and flat byte views keep their existing paths.

Supporting head-major rows would need NIXL to track a block size per group (page length, block count, block-ID mapping and handshake). That is left as a follow-up if a model needs it.

#### Relevance

Today the trigger requires a backend with smaller blocks in a *separate* KV cache group; a drafter usually shares the target's group, so the runner picks the smaller block there too. #64611 (`--draft-kv-pool`) puts DFlash/DSpark drafters in their own group and pool, which makes this geometry the common case for MLA targets.

#### Validation

New CPU tests in `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_desc_geometry.py` make NIXL pick 64-token blocks while the group keeps a 128- or 256-token kernel block:
- `test_token_major_kernel_rows_split_into_transfer_blocks`: MLA, sliding-window MLA and attention in `LBNHC` register one dense region per layer; the full descriptor list is checked.
- `test_head_major_kernel_rows_larger_than_transfer_block_rejected`: attention in `LBHNC` with 4 heads raises.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Quantization] Keep checkpoint-excluded routed experts unquantized under moe_wna16
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`--quantization moe_wna16` handed every routed-experts layer a WNA16 method, including layers a GPTQ checkpoint stores unquantized, so loading the MTP draft of a partially quantized checkpoint failed with `AttributeError: 'RoutedExperts' object has no attribute 'w2_weight'`. Fixes #36954, supersedes #39475.

`MoeWNA16Config` only knew `modules_to_not_convert`; it now also reads the checkpoint's `dynamic` rules and `modules_in_block_to_quantize`, the predicates AutoGPTQ uses since #49539.

## Claims

- routed experts the checkpoint declares unquantized get `UnquantizedFusedMoEMethod` instead of `MoeWNA16Method`, with AutoGPTQ's precedence (a positive rule listed before a catch-all `-:` rule still wins).

## Validation

```
pytest tests/quantization/test_moe_wna16.py tests/quantization/test_auto_gptq.py \
  -k "not test_auto_gptq_quantization_method"     # 33 passed, 9 skipped
```

On `main` (same test file, `vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/` from the base commit):

```
FAILED tests/quantization/test_moe_wna16.py::test_moe_wna16_experts_follow_the_checkpoint_exclusions[extra0-mtp.layers.0.mlp.experts-True]
FAILED tests/quantization/test_moe_wna16.py::test_moe_wna16_experts_follow_the_checkpoint_exclusions[extra4-mtp.layers.0.mlp.experts-True]
2 failed, 3 passed, 26 deselected
```

| checkpoint, `get_quant_method(..., "mtp.layers.0.mlp.experts")` | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-GPTQ-Int4` (`-:.*mtp.*`, experts BF16) | `MoeWNA16Method` -> `w2_weight` AttributeError | `UnquantizedFusedMoEMethod` |
| `navispace/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-W8A16-GPTQ` (`+:.*layers\.\d+\.mlp\.experts$` listed before `-:.*`, experts int8) | `MoeWNA16Method` | `MoeWNA16Method` |
| `llmfan46/...-Native-MTP-Preserved-GPTQ-Int4` (no `dynamic`) | `MoeWNA16Method` | `MoeWNA16Method` |

End to end, `moe_wna16` forced + MTP on `Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-GPTQ-Int4`, one MI355X (ROCm rejects that flag, so it was allowed through the platform list; the same WNA16 kernels already run there via AutoGPTQ's fallback): draft `Loading weights took 0.41 s`, `Avg Draft acceptance rate: 100.0%`. On main the run only works because the MTP workaround removed in #67414 nulls the quant config for the draft.

CI: `tests/quantization/test_moe_wna16.py` and `test_auto_gptq.py` are not selected by an active step. The directory-wide `pytest -v -s quantization/` run is commented out in `.buildkite/test_areas/quantization.yaml` (and its AMD mirror) since #63608, and the remaining quantization steps name specific files (`test_blackwell_moe.py`, `test_rocm_moe.py`, `test_gfx950_moe.py`, CPU/Intel subsets). The tests were therefore run locally on a GPU host; they allocate nothing on a device and stub kernel selection.

## Details

GPTQ exporters write their exclusions as `dynamic` rules (`-:.*mtp.*` keeps a speculative-decoding draft head in BF16) and AutoGPTQ derives `modules_in_block_to_quantize` from checkpoint dtypes; `modules_to_not_convert` is the AWQ-side spelling. `MoeWNA16Config.get_quant_method()` read neither, so those layers were quantized and `*_qweight` was allocated for BF16 weights.

`match_dynamic_override(dynamic, ...)` now holds the rule matching and `get_dynamic_override(config, ...)` is a one-line wrapper, so the `-:`/`+:` precedence has one implementation and no call site changes. That precedence is what keeps navispace's int8 experts quantized. A checkpoint that declares nothing (no `dynamic`, no module list) is unchanged: `moe_wna16` does not derive the list from safetensors dtypes.

commits.pr_title: [Core][Model Loader] Add sleep/wake/reload lifecycle hooks to model loader
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose Add optional lifecycle hooks so a custom model loader can react to GPU-memory-validity transitions around `Worker.sleep()` / `Worker.wake_up()`: - `on_sleep(level)` called before `Worker.sleep(level)` frees GPU memory the loader made resident. - `on_wake_up(tags)` called after `Worker.wake_up(tags)` restores GPU memory. - `reload_weights_inplace(vllm_config, model_config, model)` called from `GPUModelRunner.reload_weights()`. Returns False by default, falling back to the existing implementation, a loader that writes weights into the model itself overrides it and returns True. First two hooks are no-ops and `reload_weights_inplace` returns `False` by default, so existing loaders are unaffected. Motivating use case: the ModelExpress loader serves weights to other workers over P2P/RDMA directly from GPU memory. It needs to stop serving before that memory is invalidated by sleep, and needs to resume serving once weights are valid again. `docs/features/sleep_mode.md` documents all three hooks under "Custom model loaders". ## Test Plan Added new tests to `test_modelexpress_loader.py`: - `test_modelexpress_loader_delegates_sleep_hooks` - `on_sleep`/`on_wake_up` delegate to the wrapped loader with the correct arguments. - `test_modelexpress_loader_tolerates_missing_sleep_hooks` - no `AttributeError` when the wrapped loader predates these hooks. - `test_modelexpress_loader_reloads_weights_inplace` - `reload_weights_inplace` delegates to the wrapped loader's `reload_model` and returns True. - `test_modelexpress_loader_without_reload_model_falls_back` - `reload_weights_inplace` returns False when the wrapped loader has no `reload_model`, preserving the generic fallback path. ## Benchmark: sleep level 2 / wake up Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct, 2 replicas. One replica is put to sleep at level 2 and woken up; on wake it reloads its weights. - **Default loader:** reads the safetensors from NFS on VAST storage. The page cache is dropped between sleep and wake, so the reload reads from storage rather than memory. - **Model Express:** pulls the weights over RDMA from the other replica. | Loader | Wake up | |---|---:| | Default loader | 49.639 s | | Model Express | **7.705 s** | Wake up is **~6.4× faster** with Model Express. ---

commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Migrate dense ERNIE 4.5 to the Transformers modeling backend and keep
PaddleOCR-VL working through a temporary `AutoModel.register` shim. Also make
the ERNIE MTP drafter use the correct ERNIE decoder layer, fixing its RoPE
layout.

Part of #67937, following the scope agreed in the issue discussion.

## Claims

- `Ernie4_5ForCausalLM` now uses `TransformersForCausalLM`; the native
  Llama-derived dense implementation is removed.
- PaddleOCR-VL now initializes its inner text model through the Transformers
  backend while retaining its native multimodal shell.
- ERNIE MTP now uses `Ernie4_5_MoeDecoderLayer`, correcting the drafter's RoPE
  layout: the previous `LlamaDecoderLayer` applied NeoX-style RoPE, while
  ERNIE requires interleaved RoPE.
- Real ERNIE backend parity, PaddleOCR-VL compile/generation, and 21B ERNIE MTP
  output/acceptance were validated locally.

This is not a duplicate. The required searches for `67937 in:body`,
`Ernie4_5ForCausalLM`, `ERNIE 4.5 Transformers backend`, `ernie_mtp`, and
`PaddleOCR AutoModel.register` found no open PR implementing this migration.
Related PRs #55081 (MTP pipeline parallelism), #60666 (checkpoint renaming),
and #61811 (PaddleOCR-VL LoRA) have different scopes.

## Validation

Implementation validation was run on commit
`3c80833f1c82a0bd930e2dab6e6fc667d8e16d9f` using an NVIDIA H100 PCIe 80 GB,
Python 3.14.3, PyTorch 2.14.0+cu126, and Transformers 5.23.0. Follow-up commit

2.14.0+cu132 found dense ERNIE and PaddleOCR-VL throughput/latency at parity.

acceptance length changed from 1.683/1.689 on `main` to 1.708/1.708 on the
branch. Full benchmark and profiler results are in
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/69087#issuecomment-7100271777.

The dense native ERNIE implementation was a thin Llama subclass with rotary
and output-projection mutations. Transformers now provides the correct ERNIE
architecture, so routing it through the existing modeling backend removes that

PaddleOCR-VL still has a native multimodal shell. Its official text config and
model exist in Transformers, but the full model migration is pending
https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/50671. The process-global

decoder selects its dense MLP. This is also a correctness fix: the previous
`LlamaAttention` used NeoX-style RoPE, but the target ERNIE model expects
interleaved RoPE. Reusing the ERNIE decoder applies the correct rotary layout
while retaining ERNIE attention and dense/MoE layer-selection semantics.

No throughput or latency improvement is claimed. Local backend validation
confirmed that the existing QKV, GLU, and RMSNorm fusions are selected, and the
change adds no new synchronization to the model execution path. The observed
MTP acceptance improvement is consistent with correcting the drafter's rotary
layout.

orchestration. The human submitter reviewed every changed line, understands
the change end-to-end, and personally ran the relevant validation commands.

Under `--root-path`, `ScalingMiddleware` returns 503 for `/api/health` and `/api/is_scaling_elastic_ep` while elastic EP is scaling, even though those paths are meant to stay up. This is the same root cause as #52794 (auth middleware), and it gets the same fix.

commits.pr_title: [CI] Allow Gemma3n GPU sync on older Transformers
commits.pr_body:
## Summary

Temporarily allow the known Gemma3n GPU synchronization in the
Transformers Omni generation test while waiting for the upstream fix.

## Root cause

Transformers' `Gemma3nTextMLP._gaussian_topk` recreates constant Gaussian
sparsity quantiles during each forward pass, causing host/device
synchronization. With `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`, this causes the
Gemma3n Omni generation test to fail.

The underlying issue is addressed upstream in:
https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/51077

## Changes

- Replace the backend sparsity shim with a test-only allowance.
- For `google/gemma-3n-E2B-it` on Transformers versions below
  `5.25.0.dev0`, set `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=warn` in the Omni test.
- Keep synchronization visible as a warning and leave other models
  unchanged.
- Remove the shim-specific backend tests and documentation note.
- Add a TODO to remove the temporary allowance once the upstream
  fix is released.

This change does not eliminate synchronization on affected Transformers
versions; the permanent fix belongs upstream.

## Validation

The original backend shim passed the bit-exact MLP tests and generation
checks, but those results validate the superseded implementation.

The test-only allowance introduced in commit `7b8c6e4519` has not been
locally revalidated by the PR author.

## Overview

Allow `DecodeBenchConnector` and `rejection_sample_method="synthetic"` on DFly speculative decoding so long-context HY4 / HY4-Flash decode benchmarks (e.g. ISL 128K / OSL 512 with controlled draft acceptance rates) can run without relaxing production P/D disaggregation guards.

*(Rebased onto `main` after #69013 removed `validate_runtime` from `vllm/models/hy_v4_flash/nvidia/model.py`, so only the DFly speculator and config guards remain.)*

## Claims

- Exempt `DecodeBenchConnector` from the KV-transfer rejection guard in `vllm/models/hy_v4/nvidia/dfly_speculator.py` while continuing to reject unsupported connectors.
- Allow `rejection_sample_method="synthetic"` alongside `"standard"` in `DFlySpeculatorConfig.apply_options` (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/dfly/config.py`) so decode benchmarks can fix per-position acceptance rates (e.g., `[0.8, 0.6, 0.5]` for `K=3`).
- Add unit tests in `tests/models/hy_v4/test_flash_decode_bench_config.py` wired into `.buildkite/test_areas/models_basic.yaml`.

## Validation

### Unit Tests

Unit tests in `tests/models/hy_v4/test_flash_decode_bench_config.py` cover `DFlySpeculatorConfig.apply_options` (`standard`, `synthetic`, and invalid rejection methods) and `HYV4DFlySpeculator` (`DecodeBenchConnector` allowed, `NixlConnector` rejected), and run in Buildkite CI under `.buildkite/test_areas/models_basic.yaml` (rebased onto `main` at `e66f080af7`).

### End-to-End 8× H200 Decode Benchmark Validation

Validated on 8× NVIDIA H200 (`Hy4-flash-FP8`) with `DecodeBenchConnector` and DFly `num_speculative_tokens=3`, `rejection_sample_method="synthetic"`, `synthetic_acceptance_rates=[0.8, 0.6, 0.5]` at ISL `131072` / OSL `512` (combined with #68365 for `fp8_ds_mla` on sliding-window MLA and #68661 for DP `passthrough` support with `--moe-backend flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl`).

**Server launch command:**

```bash
python -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server \
  --model /gpfs/rd/models/Hy4-flash-FP8 \
  --served-model-name hy4 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
  --data-parallel-size 8 \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla \
  --moe-backend flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl \
  --speculative-config '{"method": "dfly", "num_speculative_tokens": 3, "rejection_sample_method": "synthetic", "synthetic_acceptance_rates": [0.8, 0.6, 0.5]}' \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector": "DecodeBenchConnector", "kv_role": "kv_both"}' \
  --seed 0
```

**Client command (per concurrency `C` in `16, 32, 64, 128, 256`):**

```bash
vllm-rs bench serve --backend vllm --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8270 \
  --model /gpfs/rd/models/Hy4-flash-FP8 --served-model-name hy4 \
  --tokenizer /gpfs/rd/models/Hy4-flash-FP8 \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len 131072 --random-output-len 512 \
  --prompt-token-ids --ignore-eos --request-rate inf \
  --num-prompts $C --max-concurrency $C --seed 102
```

<summary>Raw 8× H200 DEP8 DecodeBenchConnector + synthetic DFly output (0 failed requests across all concurrencies)</summary>

```text

[DECODE] warmup-c16: c=16 n=16 out_tok/s=637.9 med_tpot_ms=13.08 mean_tpot_ms=12.96 p99_tpot_ms=15.34 med_ttft_ms=665.34 dur_s=1.61
```

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Fix ROCm OCR preemption logit drift with DeepEncoder GEMM
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Lower all five DeepEncoder SAM convolutions to GEMM. Use ordinary PyTorch GEMM by default and vLLM's batch-invariant GEMM with `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`. Follow-up to #68563 and #68555.

## Claims

- With batch invariance enabled, changing image batch size or order preserved the visual features bitwise on MI350X.
- The live-vision preemption reproducer produced identical raw logits across five runs on MI350X.

## Validation

MI350X, BF16, PyTorch 2.13.0, ROCm 10.0.0, MIOpen 3.6.0, `ROCM_AITER_FA`, Unlimited-OCR-2 revision `cb16b920ec2249c4b280f3aa67942e00b5099122`.

| Check | Baseline | Five-layer GEMM |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Live-vision preemption | Buildkite source `74df0d1db` on MI350X exceeded `atol=0.5` in 2/3 runs, with a `0.875` difference at index 123 | All 192 logits per request matched bitwise in 5/5 runs, with one preemption per batch |
| Vision features with `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` | — | SAM, CLIP and projector outputs matched exactly for 640×640 and 1024×1024 inputs at batch sizes 1, 2 and 4, including changed sample positions |
| Single-page vision, eager with ordinary GEMM | Native conv, `11.769 ms` | `11.679 ms` (−0.8%) |
| Single-page vision, eager with batch-invariant GEMM | Initial PR with only `net_3` changed, `13.070 ms` | `12.882 ms` (−1.4%) |

Vision timings use the median of nine same-GPU paired rounds on one 1024×1024 page without crops.

On `98c5579b`, `+conv2d` and `-conv2d` selected the expected packing paths and all five layers produced bitwise-identical BF16 outputs with batch invariance on and off. With batch invariance enabled, each path also matched the same sample at batch sizes 1 and 2. The full visual features matched bitwise on the benchmark page. The median paired global-vision latency differences for Triton versus PyTorch packing were +0.45% with ordinary GEMM and +0.19% with batch-invariant GEMM.

<details>
<summary>Per-layer latency and test output</summary>

BF16 single-image layer latency in µs. Native and ordinary GEMM timings come from the default-mode run.

| Layer | Native conv | Ordinary GEMM | Batch-invariant GEMM |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |

| `neck.0` | 38.90 | 33.39 | 39.46 |
| `neck.2` | 33.47 | 42.36 | 54.39 |
| `net_2` | 34.85 | 40.74 | 45.97 |
| `net_3` | 46.52 | 40.66 | 57.70 |

The full-file and isolated preemption tests were rerun on `98c5579b`. The full-file run used a Torch-first bootstrap and `VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING=0`. The isolated preemption test used `spawn`. The two eager batch-invariant cases and the live-vision replay used the earlier five-layer patch.

```text
DIAG_DIFF single0 batch0 0 max 0.875 index 123 over05 1
```

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Pad prompt logprobs of completions aborted mid-prefill
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fixes #68601. A `/v1/completions` request with `echo` and `logprobs` that is aborted before its prompt is fully processed returned HTTP 500 (`IndexError: list index out of range`). This pads the missing prompt positions with `None` so the request returns normally with `finish_reason="abort"`.

## Claims

- Non-streaming and streaming completions with `echo` + `logprobs` no longer fail when the request is aborted mid-prefill (partial prompt logprobs) or before the first prefill chunk (no prompt logprobs).
- Prompt positions the engine never reached get a `None` logprob, which the logprobs builder already handles (the first prompt token is always `None`).
- Complete prompt logprobs are returned unchanged (no copy), so normal requests are unaffected.

## Validation

New tests in `tests/entrypoints/openai/completion/test_completion_text_offset.py` (non-streaming and streaming, each with partial and with no prompt logprobs). They need no GPU. Run on vLLM 0.34.0 (whose `completion/serving.py` matches `main` at these lines), CPU only, before and after the patch:

```
pytest tests/entrypoints/openai/completion/test_completion_text_offset.py
  before: 4 failed, 2 passed
    E   IndexError: list index out of range                      (non-streaming, partial prompt logprobs)
    E   AssertionError                                           (non-streaming, no prompt logprobs)
    {"error": {"message": "list index out of range", "type": "InternalServerError", "param": null, "code": 500}}   (streaming)
  after:  6 passed
```

## Details

Root cause: with chunked prefill, an abort can land after some prompt chunks were processed, so `RequestOutput.prompt_logprobs` covers only those tokens (or is `None`), while the echo path builds `token_ids` for the whole prompt. `_create_completion_logprobs` then indexes `top_logprobs[i]` past its end. In the streaming path, `[*(prompt_logprobs or []), *output.logprobs]` had the same length mismatch and, with partial prompt logprobs, would also misalign the generated tokens' logprobs. A small helper, `_padded_prompt_logprobs`, pads to one entry per prompt token in both paths. The `assert prompt_logprobs is not None` in the non-streaming path is removed, since `None` is now handled.

Duplicate check: no PR references #68601, and no open PR changes these lines.

AI assistance (Claude) was used to trace the failure, write the change and the tests, and run the validation; I reviewed every changed line and the results above.

commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

On an EPD consumer, keep metadata-only multimodal items out of the engine's receiver cache, so they cannot replace the real pixels of the same media. Part of #66093, **priority 4 of 4**, a follow-up. A gRPC end-to-end run does not hit it: the Rust frontend has no processor cache and always sends the image data. It shows up on HTTP, when one server sees the same uuid as a raw image, then metadata-only, then raw again after the embedding is gone.

**Depends on #66928** (stacked): the GitHub diff shows its commit too until it merges. Only the last commit, `[Core][EPD] Keep metadata-only items out of the receiver cache`, belongs to this PR: `vllm/multimodal/cache/lru.py` +38 and `tests/multimodal/test_cache.py` +72.

| Priority | PR | Scope | Depends on |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | #66094 | Proto + Rust gRPC/chat handoff + engine-role gate | — |
| 2 | #66928 | Scheduler backstop for metadata-only items. Shared by HTTP and gRPC | — |
| 3 | #66929 | `--allowed-local-media-path` / `--allowed-media-domains` on the Rust frontend | — |
| **4 (this)** | #66930 | Receiver cache: a metadata-only item must not replace the cached pixels | #66928 |

## What happens today

The frontend (P0) and the engine (P1) keep mirrored multimodal caches keyed by `mm_hash`. When P0 thinks P1 already holds an item, it sends `data=None` and P1 uses its copy. HTTP EPD sends PD a metadata-only `image_embeds` part (just `image_grid_thw`) with the same uuid, so the same `mm_hash`, as the raw image. Embedding parts skip the P0 cache, so that item always arrives with data, and P1 replaces the cached pixels with it. P0 still counts the hash as cached.

The next **raw** request for that image then sends no data, and P1 hands back the stripped item. While the EC store and the PD encoder cache still hold the embedding nothing shows. Once both have dropped it, the engine has to encode an item without pixels:

- on `main`, the engine core dies on an assertion, taking the server down;
- with only #66928, that request fails, and so does every retry: the client sends a real image and gets a 500 until P0 happens to evict the hash.

Reproduced over HTTP with the Python frontend, Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct, an encoder and a PD with `ECExampleConnector` (shared storage):

| Step | `main` | #66928 only | This PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| encoder: raw image (writes the EC entry) | 200 | 200 | 200 |
| PD: raw image, same uuid (EC hit) | 200 `red` | 200 `red` | 200 `red` |
| PD: metadata-only `image_embeds`, same uuid (EC hit) | 200 `red` | 200 `red` | 200 `red` |
| EC entry removed; 6 other large images push the embedding out of PD's encoder cache | 200 ×6 | 200 ×6 | 200 ×6 |
| PD: raw image, same uuid | **500, `EngineDeadError`** | **500** | **200 `red`** |
| PD `/health`, then the same raw image again | down, connection refused | 200, then **500 again** | 200, then 200 `red` |

`main` engine log: `AssertionError: Expected multimodal embeddings to be a list/tuple of 2D tensors, or a single 3D tensor, but got <class 'NoneType'>`. With #66928 the log shows its warning that the item `has only placeholder metadata and neither the EC connector nor transferred KV covers it`, for a request that carried the image.

## What this PR does

`LruKeyReplicatedReceiverCache` checks `MultiModalConfig.allow_missing_mm_embeddings` (an EC consumer, or a multimodal KV consumer). On such an engine, an item with nothing the encoder can run on is returned as is, without being stored and without replacing an existing entry. Items with encoder input are cached exactly as before, and other engines are unaffected. If P0 later sends `None` for a hash P1 never stored, the existing `MultiModalCacheMissError` path applies: P0 drops its entry and the request fails as retryable. The retry then carries the data.

## Where the lines go

This PR's commit: **+110** in 2 files (~38 code, ~72 tests). GitHub shows +242 / −7 because #66928's commit is included until it merges.

| File | Code | Tests | What |
|---|---|---|---|
| `multimodal/cache/lru.py` | +38 | — | `get_and_update_features` override (~13): on an engine that accepts metadata-only items, pass only items with encoder input (or `None`) to the cache and return all features. `_has_encoder_input` with a lazily built resolver (~9), `allow_missing_mm_embeddings` read in `__init__` (~3), type-only imports (~8), docstring (~3) |
| `tests/multimodal/test_cache.py` | — | +72 | Pixels survive a metadata-only item of the same hash; a metadata-only item of a new hash is not cached and a later `None` is a cache miss; other engines cache everything as before |

## How this helps Rust gRPC EPD and media handling

Today the Rust frontend has no processor cache: it always sends media data inline, so this exact sequence is HTTP-only for now. The fix sits in the shared engine cache, so it covers any frontend that pairs a P0 sender cache with EPD metadata-only items, including a future Rust processor cache. Media handling in general gets one rule: on an EPD consumer, an item that carries only placeholder metadata never stands in for real pixels.

## Validation

```bash
python -m pytest tests/multimodal/test_cache.py -q
# 7 passed
```

`test_receiver_cache_keeps_metadata_only_features_out` caches an item with pixels, sends a metadata-only item with the same hash, then sends `None`. It checks that the pixels come back, and that a metadata-only item for an unseen hash is not cached either. With `lru.py` reverted to `main`, it fails: P1 returns the `image_grid_thw`-only item.

The HTTP sequence above was run on unchanged `main`, on #66928 alone and on this branch.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Quantization] torchao: apply each fused shard's AWQ act_pre_scale
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

torchao awq checkpoints give each linear its own `act_pre_scale`. vllm fuses q/k/v and gate/up into one weight that holds one `act_pre_scale`, so every shard of `qkv_proj` and `gate_up_proj` runs with the last shard's scale. output is wrong, and at tp=2 these checkpoints fail to load.

## Claims

- qwen3-8b awq (tinygemm int4, a100): gsm8k 5-shot strict-match 0.000 → 0.858.
- awq checkpoints load at tp=2 and match transformers (main: `ValueError: Not supported args for copy_ due to metadata mismatch`).
- `act_pre_scale` is applied by vllm, not carried on the weight, so hardware repacking cannot drop it.

## Validation

a100 40gb, torch 2.14.0+cu132, transformers 5.23.0, main e71492c20 + this pr.

new `test_awq_fused_layers_keep_each_shard_act_pre_scale`: quantizes qwen3-0.6b with torchao awq, saves it as torchao safetensors, checks that a fused layer runs per-shard matmuls, and compares vllm with transformers via `check_logprobs_close`.

```
pytest tests/quantization/test_torchao.py -k test_awq_fused_layers_keep_each_shard_act_pre_scale -v
```

| torchao | main | pr |
|---|---|---|
| 0.18.0 (ci) | `1 failed, 9 deselected in 179.74s` | `1 passed, 9 deselected, 6 warnings in 206.15s` |
| main a791dcb26 | `1 failed, 9 deselected in 174.93s` | `1 passed, 9 deselected, 2 warnings in 204.86s` |

main fails with transformers `'It is designed to support multiple models, ...'` vs vllm `'\n\n\n\n...'`.

gsm8k, qwen3-8b quantized the same way (`Int4WeightOnlyConfig(group_size=128, int4_packing_format="tile_packed_to_4d", int4_choose_qparams_algorithm="hqq")` under `AWQConfig`):

```
lm_eval --model vllm --model_args pretrained=<awq-qwen3-8b>,dtype=bfloat16,max_model_len=4096 --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --batch_size auto
```

| | flexible-extract | strict-match |
|---|---|---|
| main | 0.0190 ± 0.0038 | 0.0000 |
| pr | 0.8613 ± 0.0095 | 0.8575 ± 0.0096 |

teacher-forced nll vs transformers on the same checkpoint (207 tokens): main 7.061, pr 0.934 (tp=1) / 0.936 (tp=2), transformers 0.935. after the second commit, on a fresh qwen3-8b awq build: tp=1 0.956, tp=2 0.959, transformers 0.957.

<details><summary>official h100 checkpoints (Int4Tensor)</summary>

mslk's int4 matmul is sm90+, so on a100 i replaced it with a torch dequantize + matmul. nll, same texts:

| checkpoint | main | pr | transformers |
|---|---|---|---|
| [pytorch/Qwen3-8B-AWQ-INT4](https://huggingface.co/pytorch/Qwen3-8B-AWQ-INT4) | 12.559 | 0.932 | 0.930 |
| [pytorch/gemma-3-12b-it-AWQ-INT4](https://huggingface.co/pytorch/gemma-3-12b-it-AWQ-INT4) | 1.510 | 1.322 | 1.319 |

on gemma, main still answers short prompts correctly; only the nll shows the damage.
</details>

cost: fused awq layers run one matmul per shard. qwen3-8b awq tp=1 offline generate, 128 in / 128 out: batch 1 143.5 → 133.0 tok/s, batch 32 613.2 → 604.8.

## Details

root cause: a fused layer loads each shard with `param.narrow(0, offset, size).copy_(loaded)`. the narrowed torchao tensor shares the parent's `act_pre_scale` and torchao's `copy_` copies it, so each shard overwrites it (after loading, `qkv_proj` holds `v_proj`'s scale, `gate_up_proj` holds `up_proj`'s). row parallel loading narrows the weight along the input dim but keeps the full-length `act_pre_scale`, which `copy_` rejects.

fix (`torchao.py` only): the weight loader moves each shard's `act_pre_scale` to the layer before copying; `apply` scales the input. a fused layer whose shards differ runs one matmul per shard on row views of the loaded weight. those layers skip `convert_to_packed_tensor_based_on_current_hardware` because packed layouts cannot be sliced, so on h100 they keep `Int4Tensor`'s kernel. `Int4PreshuffledTensor.from_int4_tensor` does not carry `act_pre_scale` ([code](https://github.com/pytorch/ao/blob/a791dcb26/torchao/quantization/quantize_/workflows/int4/int4_preshuffled_tensor.py#L184-L237)); taking the scale off the weight keeps unfused layers correct there. not run on h100.

the loader also stores the scale under each id when a checkpoint loads several shards at once (tuple shard ids, as qwen3.5's `in_proj_qkvz`), and padded fused layers keep their padding rows in the last shard. tp>1 is validated above on qwen3-8b; tile-layout weights also need each rank's input size to be a multiple of 1024 (torchao pads k to 1024), so e.g. qwen3-0.6b awq still fails at tp=2, on main and with this pr.

no open or closed vllm issue or pr mentions `act_pre_scale` or torchao awq loading.

commits.pr_title: [Attention][DCP] Sparse MLA DCP: CuTe DSL A2A reduce and DCP ShardQ (Kimi K3.1 6/6)
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Purpose

Last split (6/6) of Kimi K3.1: sparse MLA optimizations for decode context parallelism (DCP). Splits 1-5 are merged (#66030, #66028, #66037, #66532, #65685), so this diff is only the DCP part. Nothing here changes behavior without DCP.

Changes:

- **CuTe DSL direct A2A LSE reduce (SM100).** Same buffers and signal protocol as the CUDA op, 2 launches instead of 4.
- **DCP ShardQ.** Extends the TP ShardQ from #63956 to DCP == TP (FlashInfer sparse MLA, SM100). Each rank pushes its KV shard of the step's prefill requests (MLA and indexer pages) into a symmetric-memory workspace (`vllm/v1/attention/ops/dcp_shardq`), then handles a slice of the prefill tokens with all heads over the gathered context. Prefill tokens skip the query all-gather, LSE combine and top-k merge; decode tokens stay on the DCP path. The workspace holds `max_model_len` tokens (plus one page per request). A step that doesn't fit runs on the DCP path as on `main`; no scheduler changes. Controlled by `attention_config.sparse_mla_shard_q` (on by default, same as TP ShardQ); needs an fp8 indexer K cache.
- **nvfp4_ds_mla + DCP** is now accepted; its chunked-context gather reads the local context.
- **FlashMLA sparse:** DCP can gather up to 128 query heads, and long fp8 mixed batches run in chunks.
- The indexer metadata no longer syncs to read DCP-local lengths back from the GPU.
- Kimi K3.1 DSA layer hooks for DCP ShardQ.

Related: #65555 is the ROCm DSv4.1 ShardQ indexer.

## Test Plan / Results

### End-to-end TTFT at 108k tokens

All three configurations used the official `moonshotai/Kimi-K3.1-Pro` checkpoint (`d9e99b0792a5`) on the same eight B300 GPUs with TP8/DCP8. We sent one streaming request at a time. After one warmup, each configuration processed the same three prompts three times each. The per-prompt columns show the median of three requests. The overall median covers all nine.

| Upstream main `418af60730` | 6.805 s | 6.803 s | 6.809 s | 6.805 s | 1.000× | 9/9 |
| Merged PR `a0e2cf4be3`, ShardQ off | 6.782 s | 6.776 s | 6.787 s | 6.782 s | 1.003× | 9/9 |
| Merged PR `a0e2cf4be3`, ShardQ on | 4.911 s | 4.907 s | 4.916 s | 4.913 s | 1.385× | 9/9 |

On the same PR commit, enabling ShardQ reduced median TTFT by 27.6% (1.380× speedup).

<details>
<summary>108k serving configuration</summary>

The main and PR ShardQ-on runs used the settings below. For the PR ShardQ-off run, we set `sparse_mla_shard_q` to `false`.

```bash

  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000 \
  --revision d9e99b0792a5e93b78ea9bea62a68167e36ddd9e --trust-remote-code \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 --decode-context-parallel-size 8 \
  --dcp-comm-backend a2a --cp-kv-cache-interleave-size 1 \
  --attention-backend FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --attention-config '{"sparse_mla_shard_q": true}' \
  --max-model-len 262144 --max-num-seqs 128 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.92 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune \
  --load-format fastsafetensors
```

Each server received the same text prompts via `/v1/completions` at temperature 0 with a 128-token output limit. Seed 3 warmed the server, followed by measured seeds `0, 1, 2, 1, 2, 0, 2, 0, 1`. TTFT measures elapsed time from request submission to the first streamed choice. A response counted as correct if it contained the expected code.

</details>

### Earlier measurements at `acd6b8af23`

Kimi K3.1, real weights, one node of 8 × B300, TP = DCP = 8, FlashInfer sparse MLA, fp8 KV cache, fp8 indexer, a2a DCP backend (CuTe DSL direct reduce), interleave 1, CUDA graphs on, no spec decode, no prefix caching. The on and off measurements used different nodes. "ShardQ off" is this PR with `--attention-config '{"sparse_mla_shard_q": false}'`, i.e. prefill on the DCP path. One run per point.

Accuracy, GSM8K 5-shot, full test set (1319 questions):

| | ShardQ on | ShardQ off |
|---|---|---|
| Accuracy | 0.9500 | 0.9507 |
| Invalid responses | 1 | 1 |

Prefill, TTFT (s) of a single needle-in-a-haystack request, median of 3 seeds:

| Input (tokens) | ShardQ on | ShardQ off | Change |

| 6.7k | 0.36 | 0.44 | −18% |

## Overview

fix #68833 

Improves `ThreadedWatchDog.dump_stack` to use `sys._current_frames()` + `traceback.print_stack` for per-thread stack output instead of `faulthandler.dump_traceback`, adding a `"(Main)"` label for the main thread and emitting threads in reverse order. Also promotes `lock`/`handler` from instance to class attributes, records `main_thread_id` on `start()`.

## Claims

<!-- State the accomplishments in a few concrete bullets: speedups, feature support, bug fixes, etc. -->

- **Per-thread stack dump with main-thread annotation.** Replaces `faulthandler.dump_traceback(file=f, all_threads=True)` with an explicit loop over `sys._current_frames()`, printing each thread's stack via `traceback.print_stack(frame, file=f)` under a `--- {name}thread {tid} ---` header. The thread whose `tid` equals `self.main_thread_id` is additionally labeled `(Main)`.
- **Reversed thread emission.** Threads are iterated with `reversed(list(frames.items()))` so the main thread appears first in the dump.
- **`main_thread_id` captured on `start()`.** Set to `threading.get_ident()` just before spawning the check-loop thread, so the main thread can be identified in dumps (vllm/utils/watch_dog.py:137).

commits.pr_title: [Engram] Back NVLink peer shards with Grace EGM
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Back NVLink Engram pool shards with Grace Extended GPU Memory (EGM).

DeepSeek Engram can use this backing directly. Qwen FP8 PLE can use the same backing over NVLink with the pool integration from [#68684](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/68684).

On four GB200 GPUs, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash's two Engram tables occupy **47.21 GiB of HBM per GPU** when sharded across the group. That placement exhausted device memory while starting two DEP2 prefill engines. Both engines served with the same shards placed in Grace EGM.

## Claims

- Move **188.83 GiB of table storage** from HBM to Grace memory across the four-GPU group.
- Keep one shared copy of the tables across both engines. Each GPU owns its local Grace NUMA shard and maps its peers' shards read-only.

## Validation

- **Full model, four GB200 GPUs.** Two TP1/DP2+EP engines served the official checkpoint with EGM. With 4 GiB of KV per rank, EGM and the per-engine host-copy baseline each completed 144 one-token requests. At 16K input and concurrency four per engine, request p50/p95 was **553/719 ms with EGM** and **563/735 ms with host copies**. The host-copy run used host-NUMA VMM for the first table and shared memory for the second.
- **Lookup replay, four GB200 GPUs.** At 8,192 tokens per GPU, p50/p95 was **0.205/0.210 ms in HBM** and **0.858/1.563 ms in EGM**. Both modes returned exact checkpoint bytes for changed IDs.
- **Regression at `e6e5373dc8`.** Pre-commit and Linux-target mypy passed. The regression used the head's Python and test sources with the build-equivalent `5020556c32` nightly native extensions. The startup tests cover error propagation and mapping cleanup, including a single-rank NVML failure.

```bash
pytest -q -rs tests/test_config.py tests/distributed/test_engram_dp_shard.py -k 'engram or peer_group or egm'
```

```text
101 passed, 1 skipped, 602 deselected, 19 warnings in 79.16s (0:01:19)
```

<details>
<summary>Lookup benchmark conditions</summary>

Both lookup measurements used snapshot `e00b32ec10` and CUDA Graph replay. The four-GPU DeepSeek test sampled both official Engram tables, with 48 IDs per token. The same snapshot includes the Qwen PLE adapter. The two-GPU Qwen test used the same official FP8 PLE table at 8,192 tokens per GPU and 16 IDs per token. HBM measured 31.97/38.11 µs p50/p95 and EGM measured 68.74/74.69 µs. Each Qwen rank ran three rounds of 100 samples per backing.

</details>

## Details

For the NVLink Engram pool from #67539, set `cpu_offload=true` for Grace EGM or `cpu_offload=false` for HBM. EGM requires host-NUMA CUDA VMM, FABRIC handles, an IMEX channel, and enough allocatable memory on each Grace NUMA node.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Store the chunk containing a partial-tail CPU hit
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fixes #69024

After a request loads a partial-tail checkpoint from the CPU tier (hybrid models), the rest of the chunk containing the hit was never stored. This PR starts the next store offer at the containing chunk.

Related earlier attempt: #61375 fixed the same skip in pre-#64286 `scheduler.update_state_after_alloc`, but it has been conflicted (`needs-rebase`) since 2026-10-29 and does not apply to the current `OnComputeStoreHandler` path.

## Claims

- After a partial-tail CPU hit, `OnComputeStoreHandler` offers the chunk that contains the hit (`num_cached_tokens // tokens_per_chunk`) instead of skipping it with `cdiv`.
- Chunk-aligned hits (all non-hybrid cases) are unchanged, because floor == ceil. Chunks already in the CPU tier are still deduplicated by `prepare_store`.

## Validation

```
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector -k partial_tail_hit_still_offers_the_containing_chunk
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector
ruff format --check / ruff check on the two changed files
```

- New test on main: FAILED (`assert 2 == (28 // 16)`); with fix: PASSED.
- Full `offloading_connector` dir (CPU-only box, accelerator cleanup stubbed): main 150 failed / 517 passed; with fix 149 failed / 518 passed. The 149 failures are identical and pre-existing on main in this CPU-only environment (e.g. "Hybrid KV cache manager was explicitly enabled but is not supported in this configuration", GPU-dependent worker tests); please rely on CI for the full run.
- ruff format/check: clean.

## Details

**Root cause:** `OnComputeStoreHandler.on_load_scheduled` set the next chunk to offer to `cdiv(num_cached_tokens, tokens_per_chunk)`. On a partial-tail hit `num_cached_tokens` lies inside a chunk, and only a tail checkpoint (not the whole chunk) is in the CPU tier, so rounding up skipped that chunk.

**Change:** round down (`num_cached_tokens // tokens_per_chunk`) so the partially-hit chunk is offered. `first_live_chunk_idx` / `final_swa_tail_start_chunk` take `min()` with / pass through this index, so they need no change.

## AI assistance

This PR was prepared with AI assistance (Grok Bot); the submitting human should review every changed line and run the tests before merging.

## Overview

Build the input embedding, final norm and `lm_head` only on the pipeline stages that use them for Qwen3-MoE, Qwen3.5, gpt-oss, Gemma 3, Qwen3-Next, Nemotron-H and Granite 4.0 hybrid. These models built them on every stage, so the other stages loaded weights they never read.

## Claims

- The input embedding is built on the first stage, and on the last stage when `lm_head` is tied to it or a drafter reuses it. The final norm and `lm_head` are built only on the last stage.
- At PP=2, each stage that no longer builds the input embedding or `lm_head` loads 0.58 to 1.08 GiB less, and the KV cache grows by 0.25% to 0.43%. Tied models save memory only on the middle stages at PP>=3.
- Greedy outputs are identical to main token for token for every model checked.

</details>

## Details

Before this change, Qwen3-MoE, gpt-oss, Gemma 3, Nemotron-H and Granite 4.0 hybrid built the input embedding, final norm and `lm_head` on every stage. Qwen3-Next built the input embedding and `lm_head`, and Qwen3.5 the input embedding, in `models/qwen3_5.py`, `models/qwen3_5/nvidia/model.py` and `models/qwen3_5/amd/model.py`. Models that wrap these causal LMs get the change too: the Qwen3-VL-MoE, Qwen3-Omni and Intern-S1-Pro language models use Qwen3-MoE, and Cosmos3 Edge uses the Nemotron-H backbone.

Following the Llama and Qwen2 pattern, the other stages get a `PPMissingLayer`, and `tie_weights` moves into the last-stage branch. Intern-S1-Pro and Cosmos3 Edge build their own `lm_head` and get the same last-stage branch.

`Qwen3MoeModel` reads `tie_word_embeddings` from `hf_config.get_text_config()`, the config its causal LMs tie by. Inside Qwen3-VL-MoE and Qwen3-Omni, `with_hf_config` (#38035) updates `hf_config` but leaves `hf_text_config` with the text config's default, which is True for Qwen3-VL-MoE.

Nemotron-H never ties `lm_head`, so its last stage keeps the input embedding only for a drafter that reuses it, such as its MTP drafter.

Converting a tied checkpoint such as Qwen3.5-0.8B to a classifier with `classifier_from_token` at PP>=3 fails on the middle stage, which has no input embedding to take the classifier rows from. Other tied models such as Qwen3-Reranker-0.6B already fail this way on main.

commits.pr_title: [Core][PP][KV Connector] Expose per-stage KV cache metadata to connectors
commits.pr_body:
## Overview This PR introduces a shared mechanism for KV connectors to access planner-derived metadata across pipeline stages. The engine core exposes one `KVCacheStage` per PP rank through `KVCacheConfig.pipeline_stages`, giving scheduler-side and worker-side connectors the same per-stage view. This keeps cross-stage metadata in the core configuration path while leaving connector-specific decisions to each connector. `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector` is the first application: it uses the per-stage bytes per block to derive a consistent offload pool size, replacing its worker all-reduce and connector-specific worker/executor RPC path. ## Claims - Make every PP stage's KV cache bytes per block, as the planner sizes that stage's workers, available to both scheduler-side and worker-side connectors. - Let SimpleCPUOffloadConnector compute a consistent pool size from this metadata, removing the all-reduce and connector-specific worker/executor RPC path added in #52921. - Preserve SimpleCPUOffloadConnector pool sizes and cache reuse behavior in the validated PP1 and uneven PP2 configurations. ## Validation Tests cover PP/TP stage metadata, draft layers, overlaid hybrid cache groups (sliding window and Mamba), and consistent scheduler/worker pool sizing. End-to-end comparisons with main show identical offload pool sizes for PP1 and uneven PP2 partitions, with CPU-hit outputs matching prefix-cache-hit outputs.
Test results and reproduction commands Unit tests on B300: ```bash pytest tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_planning.py \ --deselect "tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_planning.py::test_finalize_extensible_kv_cache_auto_max_model_len_warns_when_short[True]" pytest tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_scheduler.py pytest tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_worker.py pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_simple_cpu_offload_connector.py pytest tests/config/test_config_utils.py ``` | | result | |---|---| | `tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_planning.py` | 75 passed, 1 deselected, 17 warnings in 65.12s | | `tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_scheduler.py` | 90 passed in 37.14s | | `tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_worker.py` | 30 passed in 32.78s | | `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_simple_cpu_offload_connector.py` | 4 passed in 4.81s | | `tests/config/test_config_utils.py` | 30 passed in 136.45s | The deselected test also fails on main. New tests: - `test_pipeline_stages_describe_every_stage`: PP2 x TP2 with a draft layer on the last stage; each stage's bytes per block. - `test_cpu_blocks_follow_the_planned_pipeline_stages`: a sliding-window or Mamba plus full-attention model whose cache groups overlay, planned across two stages under a layer-outermost and a block-outermost layout. Each worker registers blocks of the bytes the planner reports for its stage and sizes the pool by the larger stage. - `test_scheduler_sizes_by_the_largest_pipeline_stage`: the scheduler, which holds stage 0's config, sizes the pool by the larger stage. End to end, Qwen3-0.6B with SimpleCPUOffloadConnector (16 GB CPU), main and this PR: 16 prompts of 1K to 8K tokens, a prefix-cache-hit pass, a prefix cache reset, then a CPU-hit pass. Pool size in blocks, the same on the scheduler and every worker: | | main | this PR | |---|---|---| | PP1 | 2179 | 2179 | | PP2, 10 / 18 layers | 1695 | 1695 | | PP2, 18 / 10 layers | 1695 | 1695 | With PP2 the stage with 18 layers sizes the pool on both stages: on main through the all-reduce, with this PR on every worker directly. In every run the CPU-hit pass loads all reusable prompt tokens from CPU, and its outputs equal those of the prefix-cache-hit pass. ```bash VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1 VLLM_PP_LAYER_PARTITION=10,18 vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B \ --max-model-len 10240 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.5 --pipeline-parallel-size 2 \ --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"SimpleCPUOffloadConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"cpu_bytes_to_use":16000000000}}' ```
Log lines, PP2 with 10 / 18 layers main: ```text (Worker_PP0) [sizing.py:35] SimpleCPUOffload: aligned num_offload_blocks from 3051 to 1695 across 2 workers (Worker_PP1) [worker.py:237] SimpleCPUOffloadWorker [CPU]: 18 tensors, 1695 CPU blocks (7.45 GB) (Worker_PP0) [worker.py:237] SimpleCPUOffloadWorker [CPU]: 10 tensors, 1695 CPU blocks (4.14 GB) (EngineCore) [manager.py:197] SimpleCPUOffloadScheduler: Allocating 1695 offload blocks (7.45 GB, mode=eager, backend=cpu) ``` this PR: ```text (Worker_PP0) [worker.py:240] SimpleCPUOffloadWorker [CPU]: 10 tensors, 1695 CPU blocks (4.14 GB) (Worker_PP1) [worker.py:240] SimpleCPUOffloadWorker [CPU]: 18 tensors, 1695 CPU blocks (7.45 GB) (EngineCore) [manager.py:196] SimpleCPUOffloadScheduler: Allocating 1695 offload blocks (7.45 GB, mode=eager, backend=cpu) ```
## Details CPU offload illustrates how shared per-stage metadata replaces connector-specific coordination during initialization. * Before: * After: With PP, a connector's worker side sees only its local stage's KV cache, while its scheduler side receives stage 0's config. Connectors that need cross-stage information must reconstruct it or introduce additional communication. The engine core already holds every worker's KV cache configuration. It now exposes one `KVCacheStage` per PP rank through the `KVCacheConfig` that every connector already receives. SimpleCPUOffloadConnector uses the largest per-stage block size to size its pool; other connectors can derive their own decisions from the same metadata. Each stage's bytes per block is the device pool bytes per block that the planner sizes the stage's workers with, so it also holds for a KV cache config builder with several device allocations.
